overall_reason: The only chart is a hero product mock whose two smoothed lines have no axis, no tick, no series name and no value, so the 'Performance Overview' graph is a squiggle that shows rising lines and nothing else.

score.reason: T-ONE-QUESTION and T-FILLER fail on the unlabelled squiggle chart (DVZ-003), T-STAT-TILE fails on the 3x and 50% tiles with no baseline (DVZ-013), and T-CHART-375 fails because the chart stays 648px wide on a 375px screen (DVZ-012).

findings.where: div.hero-dashboard > div.dashboard-card > div.chart-container > svg.chart-svg, 1440 (contact sheet #1, 648 by 200px at y299; tiles/1440-00.png)
findings.evidence: The charts table finds no axes (`axes` empty), 0 text labels and 0 value labels in the plot, no legend, and 3 line candidates with 2 markers. On the crop a solid line and a dashed line rise left to right over an orange gradient fill. Nothing names either series or gives a unit, and one marker sits on the solid line near the right edge with no value beside it.
findings.before: Two unlabelled smoothed lines under 'Performance Overview', one solid and one dashed, with no scale.
findings.after: If the mock should show the product, draw one revenue line with three y ticks ($0, $1.5M, $3M), date ticks for the 30 days, a label 'Revenue' at the line end and the dashed line labelled 'Target'. Otherwise cut the chart and keep the four KPI figures.
findings.why: A visitor reads the graph as 'numbers go up' and learns nothing about what the product shows. A faux dashboard is judged as an illustration (C48), and sample data in a mock is fine (C22), but this one shows no data at all.

findings.where: svg.chart-svg and the whole hero, 375 (tiles/375-00.png, fold-375.png)
findings.evidence: The charts table `phone` row gives the chart 648 by 200px at 375 with `width_ratio_vs_1440` 1.0 and `overflows_viewport_px` 941. The sweep's overflow hit reports that the page is 1440px wide at a 375px viewport. fold-375.png shows the headline cut at 'Turn data into' and no chart on the first phone screen.
findings.before: The dashboard card keeps its desktop width on a phone and sits off-screen to the right.
findings.after: Stack the dashboard card under the hero text at 375 and draw the chart at the card width (about 340px), with three y ticks kept.
findings.why: On a phone the chart is reached only by scrolling sideways, so most visitors never see it.

findings.where: div.hero-text > div.metrics, 1440 (contact sheet #2 and #3, y608; tiles/1440-00.png)
findings.evidence: The three hero tiles read '3x Faster insights', '50% Less meeting time' and '99.9% Uptime SLA'. The first two compare against nothing on the page: there is no 'than' and no 'per week'. The sweep already reports these as stat_band (INT-007) and invented_metrics (INT-001); this finding is only about how the tiles show a figure.
findings.before: '3x / Faster insights' and '50% / Less meeting time' with no baseline or period.
findings.after: Give each tile a worded qualifier with its baseline, for example '3x faster than [DATA NEEDED: the baseline tool or process] in [period]', or cut the two comparison tiles and keep the SLA figure.
findings.why: A multiplier with no baseline cannot be read as a quantity. Lens-integrity owns whether the claims are true.

findings.evidence: The charts table reports `effects.gradients` 1. On the crop an orange gradient fades from under the solid line to the card colour.
findings.before: A gradient area fill under an unlabelled line.
findings.after: Drop the gradient, or use one flat 10% tint under the revenue line once the line has a scale.
findings.why: A fading fill adds ink and no data. It is the chart-library default look of the hero mock.

strengths: The four KPI figures inside the mock ($2.4M Revenue, 84.2K Users, 1.2% Churn, $142 ARPU) each carry a worded label, and 'Last 30 days' gives them one shared period.
not_investigated: the data behind each chart: the capture cannot see it; only what the page shows was judged
tooltips, hover values and keyboard access to data points
charts inside tabs, carousels or menus the capture did not open
charts that animate in: each screenshot is one moment
whether a source line points to a real source (lens-integrity's)
T-HONEST-SCALE: the chart has no value scale to judge
diagram tests (T-DIAGRAM-EARNS, T-DIAGRAM-FOCAL, T-30S-BOARD, T-CONNECTORS): no diagram on the page
visitor mode inferred as Persuade (a SaaS landing hero) because there is no 00-contract.md
